# PLAN — iteration 4
## Current state assessment

The verified incumbent is timing-feasible at 7 LUTs, 9 FFs, WNS 0.553 ns, and WHS 0.135 ns. Iterations 1 and 2 tried 8-bit up-counter variants and used 10 LUTs; iteration 3 changed the comparator and used 8 LUTs. The current top’s numeric latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required; preserve its registered output and reset behavior.

## Hypothesis

An 8-bit descending phase representation may map its decrementer and duty comparison to fewer LUTs while preserving the PWM output sequence.

## Instruction for generator

Replace the up-counting `counter` state with an 8-bit phase counter that resets to `8'hff`, decrements each non-reset cycle, and reloads `8'hff` when it reaches zero. Replace `counter < {24'd0, duty}` with the equivalent `phase > ~duty`, using the current phase value so `pwm_out` retains its registered cycle behavior. Preserve the synchronous reset and output reset exactly; compare routed LUT use against the 7-LUT incumbent and require all simulation, metric-integrity, setup, and hold gates to pass.
